name: Crucible Furnace Operations Proximity Vest
description: Worn over base layers in Crucible's active smelting and casting floors, the Proximity Vest is a mandatory PPE item for any worker operating within twelve meters of open-heat sources above 800 degrees Celsius. The outer shell is aluminized Pyrotek-7 fabric, the same material used in municipal firefighting gear, bonded to a ceramic-fiber batting that provides meaningful radiant heat protection without the bulk of a full thermal suit. Crucible's safety division mandated the vest-format specifically so it could be donned and doffed quickly at zone boundaries without full kit changes. Chrome arm augmentations are accommodated via open-shoulder construction with magnetic shoulder-cap attachments; workers with full-arm chrome are issued a separate radiant sleeve add-on. The vest is bright safety-orange with Crucible's anvil-and-arc logo stenciled in retro-reflective silver across the back.
cultural_context: Crucible floor workers who've been on the job long enough develop a specific way of wearing the vest — loose at the bottom, collar flipped up — that marks them as experienced. New workers wear it exactly as issued. Supervisors sometimes don't wear one at all, a status signal that reads as confidence to some and recklessness to others.
story_hooks: A spate of heat injuries on a Crucible floor is traced not to negligence but to a counterfeit vest lot that passed visual inspection but uses substandard batting — someone in the supply chain made money cutting that corner.
A veteran Crucible worker has kept every proximity vest they've ever been issued, patched and re-patched, hanging in their locker — twenty-two years of them.
The retro-reflective logo on a specific batch responds to a narrow-band UV frequency used by Vantablack field scanners, marking every wearer as a Crucible employee in their surveillance network.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, form-fitting safety vest with bold high-visibility presence. Bright safety-orange base with reflective silver anvil-and-arc branding across the back creates an industrial, purposeful silhouette. The open-shoulder design gives it an almost tactical edge—functional but distinctly not decorative. Worn by seasoned workers with a characteristic loose-hemmed, collar-flipped attitude that signals street credibility.
physical_description.fit: Snug through the torso for thermal contact, deliberately loose at the hem for quick donning/doffing at zone boundaries. Open shoulders accommodate chrome augmentations; magnetic shoulder caps sit flush against cyberlimbs. Designed for layering over base garments without bulk.
physical_description.primary_material: Aluminized Pyrotek-7 fabric (outer shell), bonded to ceramic-fiber batting (inner lining). Same heat-resistant composition as municipal firefighting gear—rated for radiant protection in 800°C+ environments.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, almost slick aluminized surface that reflects heat and light; subtle metallic sheen under industrial lighting. Inner ceramic-fiber batting has a dense, slightly rough texture felt through the material. Retro-reflective silver branding has a grainy tactile quality.
physical_description.color_scheme: Bright safety-orange (Munsell 7.5YR 6/14 or equivalent high-visibility standard) as primary. Retro-reflective silver anvil-and-arc logo across upper back. Black binding at edges and armholes for definition.
physical_description.closures: Magnetic shoulder-cap attachments for chrome integration. Friction-fit torso seal (no zippers or buckles—speed is critical at thermal zone boundaries). Open front for quick removal.
distinctive_features: Aluminized outer shell with high radiant reflectivity
Open-shoulder construction with magnetic attachment points for cyberlimb compatibility
Retro-reflective silver Crucible anvil-and-arc logo stenciled across back
Asymmetrical hem: intentionally loose bottom for rapid donning/doffing
Ceramic-fiber batting visible at seams and edges
No front closure—pulls over head and settles at shoulders
Wear marks and scuff patterns typical on experienced workers' vests; pristine on new hires
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 functional. Issued by a major manufacturing concern (Crucible) but marks the wearer as floor labor, not management. Cost-effective PPE, not luxury.
physical_description.cultural_context: Crucible smelting-floor workers—specifically those in active casting and molten-metal zones. The vest signals manufacturing-sector employment and, by how it's worn, years of experience. A flipped collar and loose hem read as street-earned competence to other workers; supervisors' refusal to wear one signals status and risk-tolerance. Visible on Tier 3 working-class individuals in the GLMZ industrial corridors.
physical_description.condition_typical: Newer worker vests appear pristine and color-uniform. Experienced workers' vests show heat-discoloration streaking (darker orange), minor ceramic-fiber pilling at high-friction points (shoulders, armpits), faint scorch marks from thermal exposure, and a characteristic pattern of creasing from repeated collar-flips. Patches of darker, damaged aluminization from heat scarring are common after 2+ years.
